newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Key points from Yeltsin's address to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Key points from Yeltsin's address to parliament.

text.p: The following are key points from President Boris Yeltsin's state of the nation address to parliament on Thursday.
Points from Yeltsin's speech are marked **, while those from the 66-page document accompanying the speech are marked *.
GENERAL
** Russia faces heavy burden of problems.
** Already low living standards are falling.
* Economic crime and corruption threaten market reforms and democracy.
* Mafia groups are openly challenging the state.
** Ruthless fight to be waged against those who break law.
** Planned nationwide protests and strikes over wage arrears are justified and a warning.
GOVERNMENT AND POLITICS
** New faces needed in government to restore order. Changes to be announced in next few days.
* Reorganisation of government, including higher pay for civil servants, needed to remove incentives for bribery.
** No need yet for constitutional changes.
ECONOMY
** GDP to grow at least two percent this year.
** Tax reform is key economic task. Government to submit new tax code to Duma within weeks. Tax enforcement will be rigorous.
** Prices of natural monopolies such as gas, electricity and railways are unjustifiably high, exacerbating non-payments crisis, and will be regulated.
* Russia to eliminate budget deficit (except for interest payments on government debt) by 1999.
* Wage and pension arrears must be paid off.
* Shareholders' rights to be defended, corporate governance improved.
* International accounting standards to be introduced from 1998.
* Federal government will not be responsible for foreign borrowing by the regions not approved by Moscow.
* Government must bring in legislation to allow privatisation of land and trade in real estate.
* Pension system to be based increasingly on private savings.
** New Treasury, not commercial banks, to handle distribution of budgetary payments.
DEFENCE AND FOREIGN POLICY
** Russia opposes eastward expansion of NATO.
** Attempts to build European security system without Russia doomed to failure
* Military must be restructured to allow creation of a professional army.
* Russian armed forces lagging those of other countries in terms of technology.
RELATIONS WITH CIS
* Russia to pursue closer integration with other former Soviet states, notably Belarus.
* Moscow has no imperial ambitions but Baltic states must not discriminate against Russian minorities.
* Russia willing to work patiently with Ukraine to solve common problems such as future of Black Sea fleet.
